transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What's been bringing you in to see me?

Yeah, so… the main thing is I’m having a really hard time staying with things I’m supposed to be focused on. Like at work, I’ll start a safety briefing or we’re going over a plan review, and I’m trying—like I know it matters—but within a few minutes my head is already off chasing three other job problems. Then I miss stuff I should’ve caught.

And in construction, you can’t really be doing that, you know? One missed detail turns into a whole mess later. I mean, even yesterday we were talking through something and I caught myself thinking about a delivery issue on another site, and then—sorry, that’s kind of the point—I just keep drifting off when I need to stay locked in.
Thinking back, did you notice this kind of trouble staying focused even as a kid or teenager, or is this more of a new pattern for you?

No, it definitely goes way back. Like elementary school, even. My parents used to get notes from teachers saying I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, lose homework—stuff like that.

And I remember I’d rush through directions before I really understood what they were asking. I’d just want to get going, you know? Which is funny because now on a job site I’m always telling guys, “Read the plan first,” and then I’m the one who—yeah. But no, it’s not new. It was there when I was a kid.
These days, do you still notice things like feeling restless, fidgety, or acting impulsively—interrupting others or acting before thinking—the way you did as a kid?

Yeah, I do. The interrupting thing especially. Like I’ll walk up to two subcontractors talking something through, or someone’s got paperwork spread out and they’re working through it, and I just kind of jump in with my point before anyone’s asked me.

And sometimes I tell myself it’s because I’m trying to keep the job moving, which, you know, on a site there’s always a hundred things happening—but people don’t always take it that way. I can see it on their face, like I just barged into the middle of something. It rubs people the wrong way, and then I’m like, “Why did I not just wait ten seconds?”

Aside from the attention and impulsivity issues, have you had a pattern—either as a kid or now—of getting into serious trouble like fighting, breaking rules, lying, stealing, or defying authority figures?

Uh… not really that I can think of. I mean, I got in trouble as a kid for talking too much or not listening, but I don’t think that’s what you mean.

I wasn’t, like, stealing cars or getting into fights all the time or anything. I did butt heads with teachers sometimes, but more because I’d blurt something out or not follow along, not like I was trying to be some kind of troublemaker. Same now—I might annoy people, but I’m not out there breaking rules on purpose.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a longstanding (childhood-onset), persistent pattern combining significant inattentive symptoms (losing focus during meetings/briefings, mind wandering to unrelated tasks, missing critical details, rushing through instructions without full comprehension, losing homework as a child) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (interrupting conversations, blurting out points before being asked, historical difficulty remaining seated, excessive talking).
